question: Given the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & a & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, determine all real values of $a$ for which $A$ is singular. For the value(s) of $a$ found, analyze the consistency of the system $A X = B$ where $B = \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ b \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$ with $b$ a parameter.
explanation:
A matrix is singular if its determinant is zero.

Compute $|A|$:
$|A| = 1\begin{vmatrix}a & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} - 2\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 3 & 0\end{vmatrix} + (-1)\begin{vmatrix}0 & a \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix}$

First minor: $a\cdot0 - 2\cdot1 = 0 - 2 = -2$
Second minor: $0\cdot0 - 2\cdot3 = 0 - 6 = -6$
Third minor: $0\cdot1 - a\cdot3 = 0 - 3a = -3a$

So,
$|A| = 1(-2) -2(-6) + (-1)(-3a) = -2 + 12 + 3a = 10 + 3a$

For singular, $|A| = 0$
$10 + 3a = 0 \implies a = -10/3$

Now, with $a = -10/3$:
Matrix $A$ becomes $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -10/3 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

Let us check the consistency of $AX = B$:
If $\operatorname{adj}A \cdot B \ne 0$, the system is inconsistent. If $\operatorname{adj}A \cdot B = 0$, consistent (possibly infinite solutions).

You must construct $\operatorname{adj}A$ at $a = -10/3$ and multiply by $B$. If the product is non-zero for some $b$, inconsistent – else, consistent for specific $b$.

(Steps showing the cofactors and product calculation omitted for brevity. The key point is that for general $b$, the system is inconsistent unless $b$ takes specific dependent values, which can be found by setting $\operatorname{adj}A\cdot B=0$ and solving for $b$.)

options.A: $a=\frac{10}{3}$; the system is consistent for all values of $b$.
options.B: $a=-\frac{10}{3}$; the system is inconsistent for all values of $b$.
options.C: $a=-\frac{10}{3}$; the system is consistent with infinitely many solutions when $b=-\frac{16}{3}$ and inconsistent otherwise.
options.D: $a=0$; the system has a unique solution for every value of $b$.
